item.title: Andrey Zvyagintsev believes filmmakers know what the audience wants — not executives
item.description:
The year is 2022. Vladimir Putin has announced the military draft. In Andrey Zvyagintsev's Minotaur, set in the fictional town of Krasoborsk, a quietly unhappy couple, called Gleb and Galina, carry on with their lives, or try to, geopolitics notwithstanding. For Galina, carrying on means an affair, which we deduce from a scene of her texting with a faint smile, her face lit in the dark by the light of her phone. (Minotaur is a remake of Claude Chabrol's 1969 film The Unfaithful Wife, whose title gives the plot away more readily than Zvyagintsev's.)

Meanwhile, Gleb runs a kind of private contracting concern and is soon asked to scare up mili …

Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: The best early Black Friday deals you can already shop
item.description:
The countdown to Black Friday is on, and many discounts have already arrived. Although the shopping holiday isn’t officially until November 27th, retailers are already dropping early deals on some of our favorite tech. Of course, with prices rising across the board, a good discount doesn’t necessarily mean you’re getting a historically low price. But we’re still seeing worthwhile discounts on a host of tried-and-tested gear, with more expected next week.

Below, we’ve rounded up the best early Black Friday deals we’ve found so far. Prices could drop further as Black Friday approaches, as is always the case, but these deals are worth considering if you’d rather shop early and beat the holiday rush. We’ll continue to update this guide as more retailers launch their holiday sales, too, so be sure to check back regularly as we get closer to the main event.

AirPods Pro 3

Apple’s AirPods Pro 3 deliver the best noise cancellation and sound quality of any AirPods yet, along with a more comfortable, secure fit and improved water resistance. They also feature built-in heart rate tracking for workouts and support live translations for a handful of languages. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $249 $179 at Amazon
  • $249 $179 at Walmart
  • $249 $179.99 at Best Buy

Sony DualSense Wireless Controller

Sony’s DualSense Wireless Controller for the PlayStation 5 features immersive haptic feedback and resistance triggers, which feel great to use. It offers a built-in mic, a 3.5mm headphone jack, and a mute button; it also works with PC, macOS, and mobile devices via Bluetooth or USB-C.

Where to Buy:

  • $74.99 $54 at Amazon
  • $74.99 $54.99 at Best Buy
  • $74.99 $54.99 at Target

007 First Light

007 First Light, a third-person stealth action game from the studio behind Hitman, is arguably the best action game we’ve played this year. It features a wide variety of missions that have you sneaking through enemy territory, engaging in hand-to-hand combat, and taking part in high-speed car chases — you know, classic Bond stuff. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $69.99 $34.99 at PlayStation Store

Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Plus

Amazon’s last-gen Fire TV Stick 4K Plus streams in 4K and supports Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Alexa Plus. It also ships with the redesigned Fire OS and, unlike more recent models, still lets you sideload Android TV apps.

Where to Buy:

  • $69.99 $29.99 at Amazon
  • $69.99 $29.99 at Best Buy

Apple Watch Series 12

The Apple Watch Series 12 introduces AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, including sound recognition alerts, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. It can also track your heart rate every five seconds, even when you’re not exercising, and offers faster charging than prior models. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $399 $329 at Amazon
  • $399 $329 at Walmart
  • $399 $329 at Best Buy

Philips Hue Essential four-pack of bulbs

Philips Hue bulbs can be pricey, which is why the company’s four-pack of Essential A19 bulbs is a great buy at the current sale price. The adjustable bulbs offer white and color ambiance, 800 lumens of brightness, and can be controlled either via Bluetooth or a Hue Bridge (sold separately).

Where to Buy:

  • $59.99 $41.99 at Amazon (four-pack)
  • $119.99 $99.99 at Best Buy (with Hue Bridge)
  • $119.99 $97.99 at Amazon (with Hue Bridge)

Fanttik S1 Pro Cordless Electric Screwdriver

Fanttik’s rechargeable electric screwdriver features three adjustable torque settings, a built-in LED light, and 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling everything from furniture assembly to small electronics repairs. It also comes with a magnetic storage case and supports USB-C.

Where to Buy:

  • $79.99 $39.99 at Amazon

Nothing Ear 3A earbuds

You likely won’t find wireless earbuds with a more striking appearance than Nothing’s Ear 3A. They also sound fantastic, boast active noise cancellation, and offer robust EQ settings, making them a great pick for the price. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $99 $69 at Amazon
  • $99 $69 at Walmart
  • $99 $69 at Best Buy

MacBook Neo

Apple’s most affordable laptop uses the same A18 Pro chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro. It features a vibrant 13-inch display, surprisingly good speakers, and 8GB of RAM, making it a solid option for students and anyone who needs a laptop for everyday tasks. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $799 $749 at Amazon (512GB)
  • $699 $649 at Best Buy (256GB)
  • $699 $649 at Amazon (256GB)

Bose SoundLink Max SE speaker

The cheaper, more streamlined SoundLink Max features a slightly smaller battery (16 vs. 20 hours) and lacks external power bank functionality. Otherwise, it’s the same as the standard model, which means the audio is just as great.

Ember Mug 3 (14-ounce)

Ember’s latest smart mug is designed to keep your coffee at the ideal temperature for up to three hours, with five temp settings between 120 and 145 degrees Fahrenheit. The third-gen version is similar to prior models; however, you can now adjust the heat settings directly on the mug and throw it in the dishwasher, which wasn’t the case before.

  • $149.95 $99.99 at Best Buy

Flextail’s Zero Pump 2 might weigh a mere 1.7 ounces, but it can quickly inflate and deflate a sleeping pad. It comes with six nozzles and a replaceable battery that recharges via USB-C, allowing you to inflate up to 30 pads on a single charge.

Litter-Robot 4 Starter Bundle

Casetify Moonaries illo Edition 2 phone case

item.title: UN court cites military Facebook posts while finding Myanmar guilty of genocide
item.description:
In its ruling that Myanmar committed state-sponsored genocide against the Rohingya people in 2016 and 2017, the United Nations' top court says that Facebook played a role in helping Myanmar's military spread hate speech against its Muslim minority. The ruling from the International Court of Justice determined that Facebook posts made by the country's military "dehumanized" the Muslim minority "and at times encouraged and legitimized violence against them," as reported earlier by Reuters.

The decision that Myanmar committed genocide comes after The Gambia sued the country in 2019 over the military's violent "clearance operations" targeting t …

item.title: Let’s talk about GTA VI
item.description:
It's hard to believe, but Grand Theft Auto VI is now a real thing that we all can play. Thirteen years after GTA V, and eight years since Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar is back with its latest sprawling, extravagant open world. There's a lot to experience - and a lot to talk about.

Perhaps the most impressive thing about GTA VI is how flexible it is, letting you mold the experience to your own play style. You can still be a maniacal criminal, but you can also focus on the new love story that includes an entire button dedicated to holding hands. Or you can spend the hours fishing or driving around listening to the radio. Maybe you just want …

Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: The week everything fell apart
item.description:
There was a dayslong Outlook outage. A nationwide ground stop for only the second time in 25 years. Banks seemed to suddenly stop working. Even iCloud couldn't stay up and running. This week, it felt like the technological world simply collapsed. And it felt like this might be the beginning of something even bigger.

On this episode of The Vergecast, Nilay and David go through the week's many calamities, and try to explain both what happened in each case - which was generally much milder than the conspiracy theories would have you believe - and why all these small issues might still add up to something worth worrying about. In a world filled …

item.title: Signal is blocking Gemini and Siri AI from reading your screen
item.description:
Signal is restricting the ability to take screenshots on Android and iOS devices in an effort to prevent AI agents from reading users' messages and other data. The agentic AI capabilities built into operating systems that analyze on-screen information to learn more about the user are "undermining Signal's ability to independently guarantee privacy," Signal president Meredith Whittaker said in a blog post, while urging OS providers to make it easier for app developers to control what data agents can access.

"We want to be very clear: it is a serious problem that Signal - and application developers beyond - lack robust tools to prevent AI age …

Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Why the robots are ditching Uber
item.description:
In a late August earnings call, Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi sounded optimistic about his company's "very strong" partnership with Waymo, the global leader in autonomous robotaxis. The two companies had been working together for years in several cities - including exclusively in Austin and Atlanta - and things were going swimmingly, according to Khosrowshahi.

"We believe we'll continue to operate next year in those marketplaces," he gushed. "It's a terrific product, and the on-the-ground partnership continues to be very strong."

item.title: Apple is hiring engineers to build its own AI agent
item.description:
Apple is working on its own AI agent that can perform a range of tasks for you, including browsing the web, working across apps, writing code, and calling services. That's according to a now-removed job listing spotted by Bloomberg, which said Apple is looking for an engineer to lead the creation of an agentic AI assistant.

An AI agent from Apple would put the iPhone maker in the running to compete with the likes of Meta's Muse, OpenAI's Dots, Anthropic's Duet, and Google's Tasks. Muse, ChatGPT, and Perplexity can already take control of a computer through their Mac apps, while Google just started letting Gemini do the same.

item.title: A brief history of Nvidia’s recent stock fluctuations
item.description:
"We've got this," Colette Kress, interim CEO of Nvidia, said Tuesday night as she closed out the embattled chip company's third quarter earnings call.

By Thursday, the company's stock price was hovering at around $150 per share, a nearly 40 percent drop from its all-time high on October 6th, and wiping out a brief post-earnings pop on Tuesday night. Meanwhile, Wall Street was paying up for one of Nvidia's biggest customers as Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut at $111.50 per share - 34 percent higher than expected.

Looking at the earnings report numbers alone, Nvidia had a blockbuster quarter. Q3 revenue more than doubled from the same period …
